title: Elastic headroom guidelines for Dedicated POC (customer X)
content:
Purpose:
Quick reference and working notes for designing "elastic headroom" and autoscaling guardrails for Dedicated POCs. Target audience: solutions eng + platform eng when sizing reserved GPU pools for enterprise trials.

Context / problem statement:
Customer X wants a Dedicated deployment to support an interactive chat product with occasional batch embedding jobs. They need predictable latency for the chat path (99th pct <= 450ms) but also want to avoid heavy overprovisioning for weekend batch runs. This doc captures heuristics we used during the onsite workshop and a lightweight calculator to convert workload signals into a recommended pool + autoscale posture.

Workload profile (observed / estimated):
- Chat (primary): 85% of requests, short prompts (avg tokens in: 40, generated avg tokens: 120), median latency target 150ms, 99th target 450ms.
- Async embeddings (secondary): 15% of requests, bulk jobs arriving in windows (typical spool 10k docs over 2–6 hours). Embedding model cheaper per token but uses CPU/GPU for batch vectorization.
- Traffic shape: diurnal with two peaks (11:00 and 17:00 local). Occasional spikes 3–5x baseline during marketing events.

Key constraints and priorities:
- Strong SLA for interactive chat latency at 99th percentile.
- Cost sensitivity: customer expects the vendor to propose a solution that minimizes committed spend while providing graceful degradation and predictable tail latency.
- Security: Private VPC, no shared KV caching across tenants; KV cache only for per-tenant.

Sizing heuristics (stepwise):
1) Characterize tokens/s and concurrency for chat path. Baseline: 100 qps * (avg out tokens 120) => 12k generated tokens/sec. Expect batching to reduce per-token cost by ~1.8x at 100 qps.
2) Pick a model family and perf baseline. For these notes we used Llama-WS-13B quantized profile: ~120 tokens/sec per A100-40GB (serving config tuned for 1.5x throughput with kv cache).
3) Convert tokens/sec -> required GPUs: required_gpus = ceil((tokens/sec) / tokens_per_gpu_peak * safety_factor). Use safety_factor 1.3 for headroom.
4) Add dedicated reserve for tail/peak and prewarmed spare for instant scale: reserve = max(1, ceil(required_gpus * 0.2)).

Example calc (baseline 100 qps):
- tokens/sec = 12k. tokens_per_gpu_peak = 120 -> raw GPUs = 100. safety factor 1.3 -> 130 GPUs. reserve 20% -> +26 => 156 GPUs committed.
- This obviously looks high: in practice we bake batching benefits (continuous batching + prefix cache) and session affinity reduces effective tokens/sec significantly. After applying observed batching multiplier 3x, tokens/sec effective = 4k -> raw GPUs = 33 -> safety-> 43 -> reserve -> 52 GPUs committed.

Autoscaling posture templates (recommended):
- Conservative (cost-first): commit 40% of expected steady-state, autoscale upper bound = 3x committed, prewarm window = 10m, cooldown = 5m, graceful fallback: route to hosted model variant (lower-cost) at 95th pct utilization.
- Balanced (recommended for POC): commit 70% steady-state, autoscale upper bound = 2x committed, prewarm = 5m, cooldown = 3m, maintain 1 prewarmed spare GPU per 10 committed for instant absorb. Use priority routing: chat traffic prioritized over batch.
- Aggressive (SLA-first): commit 100% steady-state + 15% headroom, autoscale up to +50% only, prewarm = 2m, strict admission control for batch jobs.

Policy knobs explained:
- Prewarm window: how early we start warming extra instances when utilization predicts growth. Longer windows increase cost but reduce cold-start latency.
- Cooldown: how long to wait after low utilization to scale down. Too short -> flapping; too long -> wasted cost.
- Upper bound multiplier: safety cap on autoscale to avoid runaway cloud spend.
- Graceful fallback: routing rules to a cheaper model family or hosted pool if Dedicated utilization reaches a critical threshold.

GPU cost estimation method (simple):
- Input: GPU hourly list price (on-prem amortized or cloud hourly), committed_gpus, prewarmed_spares, expected_autoscale_hours (hours per month above committed), network/storage premiums.
- Monthly committed cost = committed_gpus * price_per_hour * 24 * 30.
- Autoscale variable cost = avg_autoscaled_gpus * price_per_hour * autoscaled_hours_per_month.
- Effective unit cost per request = (committed + autoscale monthly spend) / monthly_request_volume.

Worked example (balanced template):
- Price_per_hour (A100-equivalent) = $3.2 (amortized enterprise rate).
- Committed = 52 GPUs -> committed monthly = 52 * 3.2 * 24 * 30 = $120,096.
- Avg_autoscaled_gpus during spikes = +0.5 * committed for 120 hours/month -> autoscale cost = 26 * 3.2 * 120 = $9,984.
- Total monthly infra = $130,080.
- If monthly chat requests = 12M, effective infra cost/request = $0.0108 (excluding other infra).

Batch job handling patterns (practical ops notes):
- Prefer scheduled batch windows outside peak interactive hours. If unavoidable, throttle batch job concurrency to maintain interactive SLOs.
- Provide a burst token bucket for batch jobs that charges against a separate budget; if exhausted, queue the remainder.
- For big one-off imports (e.g., 100k docs), recommend a dedicated ephemeral cluster (spot-backed) to avoid inflating Dedicated committed pool.

Risks and mitigations:
- Mis-estimated batching multiplier -> large mis-sizing. Mitigation: run a 48h synthetic load test with representative prompts and token distribution.
- Cold-starts on scale-up -> use prewarmed spare + short-lived warm containers.
- Cost shock from uncontrolled autoscale -> implement hard upper bounds and cost alerts tied to billing account.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm which exact model family customer will sign off on (Llama-WS-13B vs. MPT-30B). Different families change tokens_per_gpu by ~2x.
- Obtain precise traffic trace (1 week) from customer to calibrate batching multiplier.
- Decide spot vs reserved for ephemeral batch clusters.
- Action: schedule load-run with infra on 2026-03-02 (owner: Ben Liu).

Appendix A — quick checklist for POC kickoff:
- [ ] Collect 7-day request traces (per-route, with tokens, latencies)
- [ ] Agree on SLOs (median, p95, p99) per route
- [ ] Decide commit % (conservative/balanced/aggressive) and document in contract
- [ ] Configure autoscale upper bound and graceful fallback policies
- [ ] Run 48h synthetic soak with golden prompts and measure real batching multiplier
- [ ] Recompute committed_gpus and present revised cost estimate to customer

Notes to self (workshop fragments):
- Tomas: customer cares more about p99 tail than monthly cost but will accept routing fallback if explicit failover path exists.
- Priya: get legal input on prewarmed spare licensing for on-prem footprints.
- Quick hack: use tokens_per_gpu of 180 for Llama-WS quantized w/ prefix caching in our baseline table (we need to validate).
